  3. When he heard an alarming sound from outside, he scrambled out of bed and groped his way to the window.
  4. On his way to the window, he groped after he scrambled out of bed because he heard an alarming sound from outside.
Answer and explanation

C. Choice (C) states the idea in the clearest way. In simple terms, it describes what he did and why. The beginning phrase in Choice (A) doesn’t properly describe the subject of the sentence, which is he. Choice (B) separates prepositional phrases from the verbs they describe, and Choice (D) is wordy and awkward.

barrons-1-113 · reading
Tyrants

In discussions of archaic Greece, a tyrant was a ruler who gained personal power outside a city’s usual constitutional arrangements. The label did not by itself tell us everything about the ruler’s character. Political strife, or conflict, could help a determined leader gain supporters. Some seized power by force; support from groups dissatisfied with aristocratic rule could also matter. Their governments were not all alike. Some tyrants sponsored temples, public buildings, and religious festivals. Such projects could benefit a city and help a ruler gain support. Yet a popular project was not the same as allowing citizens to control their government. Nor does a public building prove that its sponsor governed justly. A careful history therefore considers both the benefits a ruler claimed to provide and the concentration of power in that ruler’s hands. Concord, meaning harmony, might be an ideal people desired, but it should not be assumed that every tyrant created lasting peace. The useful question is not whether every tyrant was wholly good or wholly bad. It is how a particular ruler acquired power, used it, and affected the people of the city.

What defines a tyrant in the historical discussion here?

  1. a ruler elected under every ordinary rule
  2. a ruler gaining personal power outside usual constitutional arrangements
  3. any poet
  4. any temple builder
Answer and explanation

B. The opening sentence defines the political use of the term.

The label did not by itself tell us everything about the ruler’s character. Political strife, or conflict, could help a determined leader gain supporters. Some seized power by force; support from groups dissatisfied with aristocratic rule could also matter. Their governments were not all alike. Some tyrants sponsored temples, public buildings, and religious festivals. Such projects could benefit a city and help a ruler gain support. Yet a popular project was not the same as allowing citizens to control their government. Nor does a public building prove that its sponsor governed justly. A careful history therefore considers both the benefits a ruler claimed to provide and the concentration of power in that ruler’s hands. Concord, meaning harmony, might be an ideal people desired, but it should not be assumed that every tyrant created lasting peace. The useful question is not whether every tyrant was wholly good or wholly bad. It is how a particular ruler acquired power, used it, and affected the people of the city.

Which claim does the author reject?

  1. Tyrants could sponsor festivals.
  2. Every tyrant created lasting peace.
  3. People could desire harmony.
  4. A ruler could concentrate power.
Answer and explanation

B. The text warns readers not to assume universal lasting peace.

barrons-1-123 · reading
Perennials

A gardener can choose from a plethora of perennial plants. A perennial lives for more than two years, although its actual lifespan depends on the plant and growing conditions. In many herbaceous perennials, aboveground growth dies back during a dormant season while living underground structures allow new growth later. This does not mean that the plant’s roots die every year or that the plant will live forever. Perennials can return without planting a new individual each year, but they still need suitable light, soil, and water to thrive. Some prefer sun; others suit shadier places. In this sample garden plan, the gardener chooses perennial hostas for leafy growth in shade and Shasta daisies for a sunny bed. She also plants annual zinnias. Annuals complete their life cycle in one growing season; seedlings appearing later are new plants. Different plants flower at different times. Mixing annuals and perennials is one way to extend the garden’s season of color, because annual flowers can fill gaps between perennial blooms. It is an option, not a rule that every successful garden must follow. Planning for local conditions and flowering times is more useful than assuming that any plant needs no care.

What is a possible benefit of perennials?

  1. They live only one year.
  2. They require no light.
  3. They never need water.
  4. They can return without planting a new individual each year.
Answer and explanation

D. The benefit is returning growth under suitable conditions, not guaranteed survival without care.

barrons-1-133 · reading
Crickets

Have you ever wondered why or how crickets make that unique chirping sound? Only the male crickets can chirp. This chirping is a means of attracting a female cricket with a loud and constant sound. The same sound also sends a message to other male crickets to stay away. Crickets are nocturnal insects, so their chirping is an important way of letting other potential mates know where to find them during the night. It has long been known that there is a relationship between the frequency of chirps and the outside temperature. For over one hundred years, people have been counting the number of cricket chirps in a time interval and using this to estimate the temperature. One method instructs listeners to count the number of chirps in a 14-second interval and add 40. This will yield an approximate temperature in degrees Fahrenheit. Some methods suggest adding 38 rather than 40, while other methods suggest using an interval of 15 seconds. The formula for converting to degrees Celsius is a little more complicated. The variety of methods is a reminder that this is not an exact science but rather an estimate of the actual temperature. So how do crickets manage to create such a unique sound? Male crickets chirp by rubbing an edge of their wing against ridges on the other wing. The exact sound depends on the number of ridges and the distance between them. So the next time you hear that summer sound of chirping crickets, you'll be able to estimate the temperature while appreciating the conversation.

Crickets make a chirping sound

  1. to attract other male crickets.
  2. to let humans know the temperature.
  3. so they don't get stepped on by people.
  4. to attract a mate.
Answer and explanation

D. first paragraph says attract a mate

Male crickets chirp by rubbing an edge of their wing against ridges on the other wing. The exact sound depends on the number of ridges and the distance between them. So the next time you hear that summer sound of chirping crickets, you'll be able to estimate the temperature while appreciating the conversation.

The best title for this passage is

  1. "The Curious Sounds of Crickets."
  2. "Global Warming and Crickets"
  3. "How to Find a Cricket."
  4. "Research Findings of Grasshoppers."
Answer and explanation

A. title covers sounds and their uses
